skill.name: gjalla-spec
skill.description: Create a well-thought-out plan covering problem statement, goals, technical approach, and verification criteria. Use while planning / before implementing any non-trivial feature.
skill.summary: Create implementation-ready software specifications grounded in architecture, constraints, source code, and measurable verification criteria.
skill.author: gjalla

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a false positive caused by Markdown backticks around a Gjalla CLI command. The prompt contains no executable code, prompt injection, or malicious intent.

static_findings.snippet: When you have everything you need, go ahead and use `gjalla spec new` which will scaffold a change s

finding_verdicts.reason: The backticks on line 14 are Markdown inline-code delimiters around the literal command `gjalla spec new`. They are not Ruby or shell command-substitution syntax and cannot execute within SKILL.md.

content.value_statement: Complex features fail when requirements, architecture effects, and verification criteria remain unclear. This skill guides agents through research and produces an implementation-ready Gjalla specification.
actual_capabilities: Guides retrieval of relevant architecture, capabilities, data flows, and rules from Gjalla.
Directs focused source code research after the current system state is understood.
Identifies unresolved decisions and requests user input before proposing a solution.
Structures problem, goals, non-goals, requirements, technical approach, dependencies, rollback, and verification.
Guides creation of a canonical change specification with the Gjalla CLI.
limitations: Requires access to a configured Gjalla CLI or MCP integration for repository specifications.
Does not implement the planned feature or verify that implementation matches the specification.
Plan quality depends on available architecture records, source code, and user answers.
The documented Gjalla command may create files in the active workspace.

use_cases.title: Plan a Cross-Service Feature
use_cases.description: Map architecture effects, data flows, dependencies, rollback steps, and tests before changing multiple services.

use_cases.title: Define Acceptance Criteria
use_cases.description: Turn a product problem into explicit goals, non-goals, observable behaviors, and acceptance tests.

use_cases.title: Prepare an Implementation Handoff
use_cases.description: Create a concise reference specification that gives delivery teams shared technical and verification guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Feature Specification
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Gjalla specification for [feature]. Research the current architecture, ask necessary questions, and define goals, requirements, approach, tests, dependencies, and rollback.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a defined feature that needs structured planning.

prompt_templates.title: Clarify an Ambiguous Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate the current system around [problem]. Identify missing decisions, ask focused questions, then draft a specification with explicit non-goals and verification criteria.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when requirements are incomplete or conflicting.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a System Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan the migration from [current state] to [target state]. Cover architecture deltas, data flows, sequencing, dependencies, compatibility, verification, and rollback.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for migrations that affect data, services, or deployment order.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Second-Order Effects
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an advanced change specification for [proposal]. Trace downstream effects, failure modes, operational risks, boundary constraints, phased delivery, acceptance tests, and rollback triggers.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for high-impact changes with broad technical consequences.

output_examples.input: Plan account deletion across authentication, billing, and analytics services.
output: Problem: Account deletion behavior is inconsistent across services.
Goal: Remove personal data while preserving legally required billing records.
Approach: Coordinate deletion events, retention rules, retries, audit records, and service ownership.
Verification: Test complete deletion, partial failures, retries, retention exceptions, and rollback.

output_examples.input: Specify a gradual migration from synchronous notifications to a queue.
output: Non-goal: Replacing notification providers is outside this migration.
Architecture delta: Producers publish durable jobs while workers handle delivery and retries.
Dependencies: Queue infrastructure, observability, idempotency keys, and deployment sequencing.
Rollback: Route producers back to synchronous delivery while safely draining queued jobs.

best_practices: Provide the problem, affected systems, constraints, and relevant Gjalla project context.
Resolve decisions that change the technical approach before approving the specification.
Make every behavioral requirement observable and pair it with a verification method.
anti_patterns: Do not approve a specification that assumes undocumented architecture or missing dependencies.
Do not combine goals, implementation details, and verification into vague narrative paragraphs.
Do not omit rollback planning for changes that affect production data or shared services.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces a structured change specification covering the problem, scope, requirements, technical approach, verification, dependencies, and rollback.

faq.question: Does it require Gjalla?
faq.answer: Yes. Its intended workflow uses Gjalla CLI or MCP to retrieve project context and create the canonical specification.

faq.question: Will it implement the feature?
faq.answer: No. It prepares the approved plan before implementation begins.

faq.question: Can it use Claude Plan or another plan format?
faq.answer: Yes. It can present an alternative planning format, then record approved information in a Gjalla specification.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it before non-trivial features, migrations, architectural changes, or work with important dependencies and rollback requirements.

faq.question: How does it handle missing information?
faq.answer: It researches available specifications and source code, then asks focused questions that affect the proposed solution.
